In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of signal transduction and synaptic transmission in the retina.
the function of the retina and the molecular mechanisms that underlie its function.
the molecular identity of the transducing channel at the synapse between rod photoreceptors and rod bipolar cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transduction current of rod bipolar cells is mediated by a TRP-like cation channel, possibly TRPV1 or TRPM1.
TRPV1 is not the channel that couples the mGlu6 receptor to the transduction current.
the metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR6) in rod bipolar cells is coupled to a TRP-like transduction channel that is likely to be TRPM1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a TRP channel is the synaptic cation channel in On bipolar cells.
the TRP-like channel is the transduction channel for rod bipolar cells.
the transduction current in rod bipolar cells is likely to be mediated by a member of the transient receptor potential family of channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a member of the large TRP channel superfamily mediates synaptic function in rod bipolar cells.

the transduction current is mediated by a member of the transient receptor potential (TRP) family of cation channels, a large and diverse group of ion channels with a wide variety of physiological functions.
